- The difference between the longitudes of the two places is \( 105^\circ - 56^\circ = 49^\circ \).

- 196 minutes = 3 hours and 16 minutes.
- As both A and B marked places are located in the west longitude, the time of B marked place will be advanced than A marked place. As B marked place is located to the east of A marked place, the B marked place will have an advanced time.

Give reasons in favor of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"The length of the day and night for A and B marked places on 22nd June will not be the same.
- Due to the annual motion of the Earth, the length of both days and nights increases and decreases. The Earth moves round the Sun continuously on its own axis through a certain semi-circular orbit, to a certain direction and duration. Such rotation of Earth to the east from the west is called the ‘Annual Motion’. While moving round the Sun, the north poles inclines towards the Sun at one point of time. At another time, the south pole inclines towards the Sun. Length of the day for the pole getting inclined towards the Sun gets longer than the night and vice versa happens for the other pole where days become shorter and nights longer.
- The A marked place mentioned in the stem is located at 30° north Axis meaning it is located in the northern hemisphere. The B marked place is located at 50° south Axis, meaning in the southern hemisphere. On June 22nd, the North Pole get inclined towards the Sun and the south pole remains farthest away from the Sun. As the sunlight falls over this place lengthways, the day on this date becomes the longest in the north hemisphere and the night becomes the shortest. The opposite situation exists in the south hemisphere.
- From the above discussion, it can be said that the two places will have opposite length in day and night time on 22nd June as the places are located in two different hemispheres and due to the annual motion of the Earth.

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is a leap year? Explain.","marks":1,"answer":"When there are 366 days in a year, that year is called a Leap Year. The time required for the Earth to make one complete rotation around the Sun is called the solar year. Usually, a solar year is calculated on 365 days but the exact time is 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45°-51 seconds. That’s why every fourth English year is calculated with an additional day, i.e. 366 days. In that year, February possesses 29 days instead of 28. Such a year is called the ‘Leap Year’.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"When did Mysha talk to as per the local time of Canberra?","marks":2,"answer":"The stem mentioned that the meridian of longitude of Sweden is 15° east and Canberra is 150° east.
- The difference of longitude between the two places is \( 150^\circ - 15^\circ = 135^\circ \).
- For every 1° difference of longitude, the time difference is 4 minutes. So, for 135° difference of longitude, the time difference will be \( 135^\circ \times 4 = 540 \) minutes.
- 540 minutes = 9 hours.
- As both Sweden and Canberra are located at east longitude, Canberra will have an advanced time than Sweden. Canberra is located in the east of Sweden. That’s why it will be far ahead in time than Sweden.
- The difference of time between Sweden and Canberra is 9 hours.
- The time given for Sweden in the stem is 6 in the morning so, the local time for Canberra will be 6 AM + 9 hours = 3 in the afternoon or 3 P.M.

- Sweden is located at 66.5° north axis meaning it is located in the northern hemisphere. On the other hand, Canberra is located in the southern hemisphere, at 35° south axis. On December 22nd, the last day of the Winter solstice, the sunlight falls lengthways (90°s) towards the Tropic of Capricorn. On this date, the day becomes the longest and the night shortest in the south hemisphere. One and a half months before and after this date, it remains summer in the south hemisphere and winter in the northern hemisphere.
- Maliha will go to Sweden on 28th December. We know that one and a half months prior and after the date of 22nd December, it remains summer in the south and winter in the north hemisphere. As Sweden is located in the north hemisphere and Canberra in the south, that’s why, on the date of Maliha’s travel, it will not be the same season in these two places.

Due to the rotation of the earth and the moon, the influence of the Centrifugal Force affects the oceans too.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the reasons why such reaction was held in the seawater then.","marks":3,"answer":"The reason for the reaction that Synthia observed in the ocean is known as ebb and flow. Inflation of the seawater in a regular course is called the high tide or flow and descending thereof is called the low tide or ebb. Scientists now-a-days have proved that the high and low tides occur in consequence of the centric force generated due to the Earth’s rotation and attraction from the Sun and the Moon over the Earth.
- Each substance of the Earth has an attraction and one attracts the other. This attraction is called the gravitation force or the gravity. Due to the gravity, the Earth moves round the Sun, and the Moon moves round the Earth. One that is larger possesses greater gravitational force. But when the distance becomes far, the gravity becomes weak. Though the Sun is larger in size than the Moon by 2.60 crore-fold but the distance of the Sun from the Earth is comparatively more than the distance of the Moon. That’s why, the attraction force of the Moon over the Earth is more than that of the Sun by twofold. Thus the Moon’s attraction causes ebb and flow.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Does the incident seen by Synthia have any effect on the economic activities of the human beings?","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, tide and flow observed by Synthia have both direct and indirect influence on the economic activities of human beings.
- Tidal Energy: Two high tides and two low tides occur during every 24-hour period. The predictability of the tides, fast movement of water during the inflow and outflow can provide a source of renewable energy to communities living along the coast. Hydroelectric plants can exploit the water flow in ways similar to those used on rivers.
- Weather: Tides and tidal currents affect the weather by stirring the ocean waters. The stirring produces more predictable and habitable climate conditions and balances temperatures on the planet.
- Navigation: Tides affect the depth and currents in and around coastal areas. Ships may need to navigate the waters during high tide in some areas or risk running aground. Due to the swelling of the river water during high tide, big ships, vessels of the oceans can easily enter the rivers and can go back to the ocean with the ebb.
- Tidal Zone Foods: Crabs, mussels, snails, seaweed and other edible sea life inhabit the tidal zone. Small tide pools may also contain small fish and sea vegetables. The sea life found in these regions are often harvested for food. Without the regular washing of the tides, these complex and abundant creatures would die and food resources would diminish.
- Fishing: Fish may concentrate during ebb tides. Commercial fishermen follow the tides and learn to hunt during levels of highest concentration to improve their economic investment and to make more efficient use of their time. Tides affect other aspects of oceanic life, including the reproductive activities of fish and ocean plants. Floating plants and animals ride the tidal currents between the breeding areas and deeper waters. The tides help remove pollutants and circulate nutrients ocean plants and animals need to survive.
- Salt production: By enclosing tidal saline water, salt is also produced in some coastal countries.
- In Bangladesh, while the depth of river extends at the Chattogram and the Mongla ports during tide, big vessels can easily enter or leave the port. Salt is also produced from drying the enclosed sea-water. That’s why it can be said that the ebb and flow have great influence on economic activities of human beings.

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The role of the International Date Line in erasing time discontinuities is immense. It is visualized as a line extending north-south entirely across the water surface area, adopting the 180° meridian. This is called International Date Line. When traveling long distances to east or west from a particular location, we can see the local time differences as well as date or time discrepancies. This problem occurs when crossing 180° longitude east or west from a place. To solve this problem, if someone traveling east crosses 180° east longitude or the International Date Line, one day must be subtracted from the local date and time. Again, if someone traveling west crosses 180° west longitude or the International Date Line, they have to add a day to their time. This eliminates the date and time discrepancies.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"When the time in X-indicated place is Saturday 8:00 am, determine the time in Y-indicated place.","marks":3,"answer":"The longitude of place 'X' is 80° West and place 'Y' is 80° East.

- Again, 1° difference in longitude causes a difference of = 4 minutes

- The place 'Y' is east of place 'X' according to the longitude given in the diagram. So, the time at 'Y' place will be more than at 'X' place. That's why, 10 hours 40 minutes will be added to the time at 'X' place.

Due to Earth's annual motion, as the places are located in opposite hemispheres, the temperature will vary in the two places.
- The seasons change due to the four positions of the earth as it moves around the Sun. Because of the annual motion of the earth, the sun's rays are sometimes perpendicular and sometimes oblique when they fall on Earth. Vertically incident rays penetrate less air and heats the surface more. And obliquely incident rays penetrate more air layers and the surface warms less as the air seeps in and spreads more widely. Due to the perpendicular and diagonal incidence of sun rays at different places, the temperature varies from place to place.
- Four positions are specified in the Earth's orbit as it revolves around the Sun. Namely- 21st March, 21st June, 23rd September, 22nd December. On March 21st, the sun shines perpendicular to the equator, so three months are spring in the northern hemisphere and autumn in the southern hemisphere. Again, on September 23rd, there is an opposite incident in the northern and southern hemispheres. On June 23rd, the Sun radiates perpendicularly on the Tropic of Cancer. During this time, there is summer in the northern hemisphere and winter in the southern hemisphere. Similarly, on 22nd December, opposite seasons prevail again in the northern and southern hemispheres. So, when it is summer in the 'Y' hemisphere, it will be winter in the 'Z' hemisphere. Therefore, the temperature will vary.
- From the above discussion, we can understand that there will be a temperature variation between the 'Y' and 'Z' locations due to them being in different hemispheres.

As a result of the attraction of the moon and the sun, the water on the surface of the earth rises at certain intervals every day in one place and falls in another. This rise and fall of water is called tide or the ebb and flow. - Salt cultivators in the coastal areas during high tide make salt by confining sea water and drying it.
- However, during strong tides, accidents also occur due to carelessness, resulting in extensive damage to boats, steamers, ships and other property.

- Because of the annual motion of Earth, the sun's rays fall sometimes perpendicularly and sometimes diagonally on the Earth, and the changes the day-night cycle takes place. This change at different times on Earth is called the changing of seasons.
- From June 21 onwards, the sun's rays fall perpendicularly on the Tropic of Cancer, thus summer is seen uniformly in the northern hemisphere and winter prevails in the southern hemisphere as the Sun falls obliquely on Tropic of Capricorn.

- To the opposite of the major tide, the landside below the water is firmly tied with the Earth’s centre, because of which an attraction of the moon over there remains equal in comparison with that of the centre. Give arguments in favor of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"Picture-2 of the stem indicates the Ebb and Flow. The tides have both positive and negative influences on the living of coastal people of Bangladesh.
- The Ebb and Flow occur due to the attraction of the Sun and the Moon. Picture-2 indicates the Ebb and Flow.
- Positive Influences:
- Due to the regular occurence of the Ebb and Flow, the sweepings existing in the river get cleansed and its water becomes free of filths and dirts, and slits gathering at the river channel or river-mouths hinder the flow.
- The river-pits become deeper due to the current of Ebb and Flow.
- The tide of water is kept confined by cutting canals beside a number of rivers for the irrigation purpose. Hydro-electricity is generated at lots of rivers in the world by utilizing the tide. There is a hydro-electricity center at Bandala Port of India.
- Due to the increase of river water during flow, big ships, vessels of the ocean can easily enter the rivers. In Bangladesh while the depth of river extends at the Chattogram and the Mongla Ports during the tide, big vessels can easily enter and leave the port.
- Salt is also produced from the sea-water keeping confined through drying process.
- In this way, the Ebb and Flow positively influence the living of coastal people.
- Negative Impacts:
- Though the Ebb and Flow have lots of benefits, these have some negative impacts. The sea-water largely enters the land-site passing through the river-channel during the spring tide in strong waves, and causes Tidal Bore.
- The Meghna, the Vagirothi, the Amazon etc. rivers become usually succumbed with the excessive tidal bore. A havoc wear and tear including submersion of boats, steamers, ships etc. inadvertently happen due to such tidal bore from time to time.
- Apart from this, due to entrance of saline water into the land surface, agricultural activities are hampered.
- From above discussion, it can be said that the Ebb and Flow have both positive and negative impacts on the lives of coastal people of Bangladesh.

- The difference of Meridians of place ‘A’ and ‘B’ is \( (15^\circ + 110^\circ) = 125^\circ \).
- We know, For 1° meridian difference, the time difference is 4 minutes.
- So, for 125° meridian difference, the time difference is \( (125 \times 4) \) minutes = 500 minutes = 8 hours 20 minutes.
- According to the table, place ‘B’ is situated on the East of place ‘A’. Therefore time will be more at place ‘B’ than place ‘A’.
- If it is 4.00 AM at place ‘A’, the time at place ‘B’ is 4:00 AM + 8 hours 20 minutes = 12.20 PM.
- So, the time at place ‘B’ is 12.20 PM.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the reason of differences in temperature between place ‘A’ and place ‘B’.","marks":4,"answer":"In the stem, place ‘A’ is situated in the north hemisphere whereas place ‘B’ is situated in the south hemisphere. Due to being located in different hemispheres and the annual motion of the Earth, there are differences in temperature between these two places.
- While moving round the Sun, seasons change at the four stays of the Earth. Due to the influence of the annual motion, the sunrays fall lengthwise in some places, whereas obliquely in other places.
- Since the sunrays fallen lengthwise reach by cleaving less layers of air, they make the surface more heated, and the rays fallen obliquely do not reach by cleaving more layers of air only, but they get extensively spread out in comparison to the rays fallen lengthwise. Consequently, temperature all over the surface varies at different times of the year.
- On 21st June, as mentioned in the stem, the sunrays fall lengthwise towards the Tropic of Cancer due to summer solistice. As a result, days become the longest in north hemisphere at that time and the heat prevails much. On the other hand, since the sunrays fall obliquely in the south hemisphere at the same time, the days become shorter and heat prevails less.
- From the above discussion, it can be said that due to the annual motion of the Earth, at the same time, in fact on 21st June, temperature differs in place ‘A’ and place ‘B’.
